correctness.rationale: The planar closest-face analysis yields vertex-vertex, vertex-edge, or parallel-edge separation. Integer determinants relative to primitive edge vectors bound every positive support-line gap below by 1/sqrt M; a modular inverse constructs an integer vertex with determinant one and projection strictly inside a maximizing segment. Equalities force primitive maximizing directions and adjacent lattice support lines. The 28t,36t family proof checks coprimality, all possible boundary deficits, and the positive differences 88t-7, 40t-7. The delivered checker has been executed and confirms 25 small rectangular cases by exact exhaustive point-segment arithmetic plus four interior-family examples. Finite checks are supplementary, not proofs for all dimensions/parameters.

value.rationale: The all-parameter rectangular kissing-distance classification is a natural shape-sensitive extension of the established cubical lattice-polytope distance problem, tied to alternating projection and facial-distance complexity. The result gives an exact finite arithmetic evaluation and necessary-and-sufficient geometric contact conditions. Its infinite 28t-by-36t family proves that optimal primitive vectors can be strictly interior, disproving the seemingly sufficient search only over full-side-span directions. It is not a routine substitution of k: anisotropic Euclidean rescaling is not isometric and the gcd barriers cause nontrivial arithmetic regimes.
